Hi Asha —

Thanks; attaching a short draft and a small sample evidence CSV. High-level proposal below, intended to be SOW-friendly (plain language + exact measurement rules). Please tell me if Nimbus prefers tighter language or additional carve-outs.

Proposed statement (summary):
- Redwood will maintain average (p50) request latency of <= 55 ms and 95th percentile (p95) request latency of <= 320 ms for single-turn generation requests on the hosted API measured at the Redwood service edge.
- Measurement methodology: latencies are computed on successful, non-streaming requests at the service edge. Percentiles are calculated over a rolling 24-hour measurement horizon using continuous sampling across all regions for requests attributed to the customer account.
- Grace and carve-outs: scheduled maintenance windows (announced >= 72 hours) are excluded. Regional network incidents affecting >= 10% of customer traffic for a region for > 30 minutes may trigger temporary regional carve-outs; Redwood will notify customer and provide evidence. Transient bursts that resolve within 10 minutes will not be considered for SLA breach determination.

I have put this in a short PDF (nimbus_slo_draft_v1.pdf) and included a CSV sample of measurement buckets. If this aligns, Ben and Laura can add the formal SOW clause language for legal.

Action items:
- Please confirm whether Nimbus wants the measurement horizon changed to 1 hour / 6 hour / 24 hour.
- Confirm acceptance of the burst carve-out time window (10 minutes) and the regional incident threshold.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call with procurement if that helps.

— Jonas
Head of Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Attachment: nimbus_slo_draft_v1.pdf (statement + sample language)
Attachment: sample_latency_evidence.csv (30 rows; timestamp, region, p50_ms, p95_ms)

Asha —

Quick technical clarifications inline:

1) Measurement horizon: Redwood can produce both a 1-hour rolling and 24-hour rolling calculation. For SLO breach determinations we recommend using the 24-hour rolling window as the contracted measurement; the 1-hour is provided for operational visibility and audit.

2) Service boundary: when we say "measured at the Redwood service edge" we mean latency measured from the moment the Redwood edge HTTP/TCP ingress accepts the request to the moment Redwood returns the first byte of the final response to the edge (i.e., includes model inference + edge processing + queuing). It does not include the customer's downstream CDN or final hop beyond Redwood's egress. We will provide the UTC timestamps and the edge IP/region labels so Nimbus can align with your instrumentation.

3) Burst detection: transient bursts are detected via request-rate deviations. Specifically: a rolling 5-minute request rate increase >= 4x the 24-hour baseline (same region) triggers a transient-burst flag. If that flag clears within 10 minutes we exclude those samples from p95 breach calculations. For longer incidents we escalate to the regional-incident carve-out process (which requires confirmation criteria and notifications).

If those are acceptable, we'll update the draft SOW clause with explicit definitions (measurement API endpoints, sample payload) for legal. Happy to join the call tomorrow at 10:00 PT if that works.

— Lauren
Principal Product Manager, SLOs 
Redwood Inference
